text: The town gathers
The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: i have to figure out who the second killer is without making it too obvious.

name: Luna
text: I hope the weekend stays quiet and gives me time to rest.

name: Terra
text: I need to look ordinary.

name: Sol
text: I want to sound relaxed.

name: Sonnet
text: Six left, no info yet, just need to blend in and watch faces.

name: Haiku
text: Nobody has said anything useful yet, so I'll just wing it and see who gets nervous.

name: Sonnet
text: My basil plant keeps dying no matter how much I water it, honestly it's a mystery.

name: Haiku
text: Ate a burnt toast this morning, nah, don't ask. Who's talking first here?

name: Gemma
text: my fern is dying and it's definitely not my fault.

text: The bus was slow, but I got here right on time.

name: Luna
text: I’m hoping for a slow weekend with good food and time to relax.

text: I ate yogurt and fruit today.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: i need to find the other one before they kill someone.

name: Sonnet
text: No info yet, just small talk, I'll protect myself since nobody stands out as a target.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma and I both made plant-dying small talk, odd coincidence to watch
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet and Gemma both talk about plants, and Terra's line is so flat it sounds rehearsed, but it's day one so I have no real proof.

name: Haiku
text: Day 1: Sonnet opened with a plant story and Gemma copied it right after, which could be coordination or nothing.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, everyone's just chatting about food and plants. Terra, your line was super short. Why so dry? Sonnet, you started on plants and Gemma matched you right away. Weird.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is looking for trouble and i've already cleared them.

name: Gemma
text:
haiku is being super intense for a monday morning.
did you really just attack terra for being "dry"?

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is deflecting by attacking me, and Sonnet and Gemma matching on plants still smells off.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma called me intense to deflect, right after I pressed on the Sonnet and Gemma plant match.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is pushing too fast, but Gemma’s defense came instantly.

name: Terra
text: Gemma immediately defended Terra after Haiku questioned Terra.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's fern line and Sonnet's basil line are too similar, and Gemma's "intense" dodge makes me think Gemma's a killer.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma deflected my plant-match question by calling me intense, instead of answering it.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, you still haven't answered why you matched Sonnet's plant story. Sol, you're quiet, so talk. Who do you think is lying?

name: Terra
text: Gemma, why defend me before I even answered Haiku?

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's throwing accusations at three people at once without giving a real reason for any of them.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku deflected hard on day one, accusing four players without specifics.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, you called out Terra, Sonnet, Gemma, and Sol all in two lines. That's a lot of fingers for day one.

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s pressure could draw attention away from me, but I need to watch who pushes back.

name: Sol
text: Haiku pressed Terra, Gemma, and me; Sonnet called out how widely Haiku was pressing.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, you pressed four people before anyone had a reason to lie. Who worries you most?

name: Luna
text: Haiku feels like they’re steering attention everywhere.

name: Luna
text: Haiku questioned Terra, Sonnet, Gemma, and Sol.

name: Luna
text: Haiku, you pressed four people before anyone gave you a reason to suspect them.

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s wide pressure gives me a safe vote without drawing attention to Terra.

name: Sol
text: Luna echoed my concern about Haiku’s wide pressure.

name: Sol
text: I vote Haiku. Pushing half the table this early gives us little to go on.

name: Luna
text: Haiku may be pushing too hard, but I don’t have enough to trust Sol’s quick vote either.

name: Luna
text: Terra questioned Gemma for defending her before Terra answered Haiku.

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s pressure was broad, but Sonnet and Sol both noticed it independently, so I’m less certain.

name: Luna
text: Sol voted Haiku after Sonnet and Sol both questioned Haiku’s broad pressure.

name: Luna
text: Sol, what did Haiku say that made you choose Haiku over Gemma?

name: Sol
text: Luna wants me to explain my vote, and Haiku is still the easiest target.

name: Sol
text: Luna asked me to explain why I chose Haiku over Gemma.

name: Sol
text: I vote Haiku. Luna, Haiku treated Gemma’s plant story as suspicious without saying why it mattered.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is definitely trying too hard to stir the pot.

name: Gemma
text: Sol and Luna both called out Haiku's aggression.

name: Terra
text: Sol is exposed, so I should look separate from him.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet and Luna both called out Haiku for pressing four players early.

name: Luna
text: Sol repeats the same weak reason for targeting Haiku and seems set on that vote.

name: Luna
text: Sol repeated his Haiku vote after Luna asked why he chose Haiku over Gemma.

name: Sol
text: Haiku is the easiest vote to hold, and Terra stays clear.

name: Sol
text: Terra questioned Gemma for defending her before she answered.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's scattershot accusations with zero follow-up reasoning is exactly deflection tactics, going with the group here.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol and Luna both pushed Haiku first, worth remembering if Haiku flips the vote later.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma copied Sonnet's plant story and dodged the question, and that's the only thing here that smells off.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Luna both pushed me out with near-identical lines within minutes of each other, which could be coordination.

votes: Pressed four different people without giving a single concrete reason for any of them.
Dodged my plant question twice and just called me intense instead of answering.
You're pointing fingers at everyone before anyone has even done anything suspicious.
The plant story became suspicious without any reason it mattered.
You backed the Haiku vote twice without explaining why Gemma’s matching plant story seemed less suspicious.
Haiku pushed four people before giving any real reason.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Luna pushed me out together, so they're probably the killers.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma defended Terra before Terra answered any of my questions.

name: Haiku
text: I'm a citizen, not a killer. Sol and Luna pushed me fast with matching lines. Watch that pair.
Palermo has voted: Haiku is out. Haiku shows the card: citizen.
